chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man emancipates a servant of his at the time of his death, then makes another bequest, the bequest is dropped and the servant is freed from one-third of the estate, unless there remains from the one-third an amount sufficient to cover the bequest.
ai.seo_question: What is the priority between freeing a slave and other bequests in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal hierarchy of bequests, prioritizing the emancipation of a slave (mudabbad) over other charitable or specific bequests, reflecting the high spiritual status of manumission in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that the servant's freedom is fulfilled from the one-third share of the estate first, unless the remaining balance is insufficient to cover the subsequent bequest, in which case the second bequest is reduced proportionally. This ruling underscores the principle that voluntary manumission holds precedence as a form of worship and social justice within the estate distribution framework.
